appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus imagines "une lutte entre votre ami et son père où il le blesserait comme David Goliath" and speaks of him striking "sa charogne, ou... sa carogne de mère", calling him a "vieux chameau" and a "créature extra-européenne".
appraisal_events.explanation: Within his antisemitic tirade, Charlus singles out Bloch specifically for grotesque, degrading mockery and fantasized violence against him and his family; the narrator's framing of these words as 'affreux et presque fous' undercuts rather than endorses the discredit.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch is made the object of Charlus's contemptuous racist caricature and imagined humiliation, though the narrator's disapproving frame limits how far this discredit is allowed to stand.

ambiguities: Charlus's flattering offer to mentor le narrateur with his 'trésor d'expérience' could be read as an elevation of the narrator, but it is bound up with Charlus's own self-aggrandizement (already captured in the accepted annotation) and its outcome is left unresolved in this passage, so le narrateur was not scored as a participant.
